trial_title: High vs. Standard Dose Rifampicin for Effusive Tuberculous Pericarditis
brief_summary:
The investigators hypothesise that high dose RIF (RIF35) will increase pericardial fluid RIF exposure and so enhance mycobacterial clearance, compared to standard of care dosing (RIF10).

This Phase 2b randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blinded trial will evaluate the efficacy and safety of RIF 35mg/kg compared 10mg/kg, added to standard first-line ATT, for the treatment of PCTB.

eligibility_table.criterion: Aged >18 years
eligibility_table.justification: age 44.0 > 18.0 → True

eligibility_table.criterion: Suspected PCTB with confirmed pericardial effusion on echocardiography (i.e., echo free space of ≥1 cm anterior to the right ventricle in diastole)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's profile indicates a large pericardial effusion, but it is unclear if the echocardiography confirms an echo-free space of ≥1 cm anterior to the right ventricle.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the echocardiography report indicate an echo-free space of ≥1 cm anterior to the right ventricle in diastole?

eligibility_table.criterion: Consent to study participation including testing for HIV-1 (if HIV status is unknown)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient can consent to study participation, and there is no indication of HIV status being unknown.

eligibility_table.criterion: Microbiologically detected Mtb in PCF or diagnosis of probable PCTB. Probable PCTB (in the absence of a positive pericardial fluid culture) will be defined as per Mayosi et al.
eligibility_table.justification: There is no microbiological detection of Mtb in pericardial fluid (PCF) mentioned, nor is there a clear diagnosis of probable PCTB.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient undergone microbiological testing of the pericardial fluid that confirms the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) or meets the diagnostic criteria for probable effusive tuberculous pericarditis as defined by Mayosi et al.?

eligibility_table.criterion: Evidence of pericarditis with microbiologic confirmation of Mtb- infection elsewhere in the body and/or
eligibility_table.justification: There is no evidence of microbiologic confirmation of Mtb infection elsewhere in the body provided in the profile.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have microbiologic confirmation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection from a site other than the pericardium?

eligibility_table.criterion: Exudative, lymphocyte predominant effusion with elevated adenosine deaminase (≥35 U/L)
eligibility_table.justification: No lab values in patient profile
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient's pericardial fluid analysis show an adenosine deaminase level of ≥35 U/L?

eligibility_table.criterion: Participant will undergo pericardiocentesis (as per clinical indication)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of pericardial effusion and may require pericardiocentesis based on clinical indication.

eligibility_table.criterion: Within 5 days of ATT initiation
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information on whether the patient has initiated anti-tuberculosis treatment (ATT) within the last 5 days.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient initiated anti-tuberculosis therapy (ATT) within the last 5 days?

eligibility_table.criterion: Glomerular filtration rate <30ml/min or renal failure requiring dialysis
eligibility_table.justification: No lab values in patient profile
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient's glomerular filtration rate currently <30 ml/min?

eligibility_table.criterion: Rifampin-resistant TB
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's profile does not mention rifampin resistance, but it is unclear without further testing.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient undergone testing for rifampicin resistance in their Mycobacterium tuberculosis strain?

eligibility_table.criterion: Severe concurrent opportunistic infection
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided about any concurrent opportunistic infections.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a documented severe opportunistic infection, defined as an infection that requires hospitalization or intravenous treatment, at the time of evaluation?

eligibility_table.justification: The profile does not specify any contraindications to the placement of an intra-pericardial catheter.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have any anatomical abnormalities or conditions that would contraindicate the placement of an intra-pericardial catheter?

eligibility_table.criterion: Failed pericardiocentesis procedure and/or failure of placement of intra-pericardial catheter
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information regarding the success or failure of any previous pericardiocentesis procedures.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced a failed pericardiocentesis procedure or a failure of placement of an intra-pericardial catheter within the last 30 days?

eligibility_table.justification: No information provided about allergies to TB drugs, so unable to assess.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a documented allergy to any standard anti-TB drugs or their components?

eligibility_table.justification: No urine pregnancy test result provided; cannot confirm status.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient's urine pregnancy test result positive?
